title: External evidence-root anchor receipt and destination certificate
purpose: Verify a W41 destination package against an independently preserved HQ root set instead of deriving expected roots from the package itself.

compatibility_hardening.description: Mirrors the Epoch 27 HQ Swift 6 parse-only allSatisfy precomputed-Bool fix; no validation semantics changed.

security_properties: expected anchor receipt root is supplied independently from the W41 package
minimum anchor sequence rejects older receipts when HQ advances the external expectation
publication ID and transfer ID are exact
every W39 run ID, workload execution ID and W39 bundle root are exact
W27, W38, W40 and W41 roots are exact as one root set
optional predecessor anchor receipt root binds a caller-managed receipt chain
destination verification composes the complete W41 verifier before anchor comparison
certificate is deterministic and explicitly NON_PARITY
adversarial_cases: same transfer ID with older W41 root

validation.mirror_note: An earlier minified Swift mirror failed because the mirror construction removed required lexical whitespace. Exact production source parse and warnings-as-errors dependency-stub typecheck subsequently passed; the construction failure is not counted as a product failure or pass.

limitations: The expectation/receipt root must actually be preserved independently by HQ; deriving it from the destination package defeats rollback protection.
anchorSequence is validated but W42 does not itself provide a globally authoritative monotonic store.
The anchor receipt and destination certificate are SHA-256 metadata commitments, not signatures or trusted timestamps.
Exact byte-for-byte re-copy of the current anchored package is intentionally accepted.
No physical iPhone, Apple/APFS durability, device-origin, real-audio or current-Moises PARITY claim is made.
